add.title: Transexuales reclusos en carceles nacionales podran optar entre prision de hombres o mujeres (AmeliaRueda.com)
add.summary: AmeliaRueda.com (Alonso Mata Blanco, 25 Jun 2017): Costa Rica's Justice Ministry (Vice-Minister Marco Feoli) announced that prisoners who self-identify as transsexual may choose whether to serve their sentence in a men's or a women's facility - relocation to the facility matching gender identity, strictly voluntary, decided case-by-case with prison social workers and psychologists; a circular ordered a census of self-identified trans prisoners, an exclusive module for trans people was under consideration, and Spain's system was cited as the model (protocols for vulnerable prison populations developed with CEJIL since 2016). Official policy-level documentation of placement-by-gender-identity in the regional context.

add.title: Stephanie, la transgenero que vive en la carcel rodeada de hombres | CR Hoy
add.summary: CRHoy (Javier Paniagua, 22 Jun 2019): Stephanie, a trans woman serving ~6 years for drug-trafficking complicity, is held at CAI Orosi de Cartago - a men's facility ('en esa sede solo hay hombres'); she transitioned while incarcerated and says prison offers 'solo hay dos opciones: o sos hombre o mujer aqui'. The Justice Ministry told CRHoy there were 23 transgender people in the national system at the time. Stephanie recounts identity-targeted abuse including a broomstick-handle rape at La Reforma (Alajuela) witnessed by a custodian. Shows that despite the 2017 choice policy, trans women were still found in men's facilities in 2019 and faced violence with custodial inaction.
